audit.whatIsWrong: Three chart rows disagreed with the packet and the already-audited mirror, and TRICKY 7/10 sat on a 52.66% lane.
audit.why: Mirror and packet both read Skill / Jax / Jax / Sylas / Sylas / Jax / Skill; my layers gave Skill on 4-5 and 6 and Jax at two items.
audit.corrected: Rows 3, 4 and 6 flipped in both layers as one atomic group; diff EVEN 5.5/10 with the even tone token.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 spike had no numbers and used a fabricated ultimate name.
audit.why: Grandmaster-at-Arms is 110/100/90 against Hijack at 80/55/30 — you hold his resist buff and re-arm it more often than he can. 'Grandmaster's Might' is not the ability's name.
audit.corrected: Real name and both cooldowns written into whys[4], spikes[0], mid, wants.you[1] and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page's core instruction was to 'hook him mid-Counter Strike so the pull stuns him out of his dodge'. That mechanic does not exist twice over.
audit.why: Riot's Abscond text gives a dash whose recast pulls Sylas to the enemy — no CC, so nothing interrupts anything. And Counter Strike 'dodges all incoming attacks', i.e. basic attacks; your Chain Lash and Kingslayer still land through it. The real counterplay is the opposite of what the page said: hold autos, keep casting spells, and leave the 300-unit stun radius.
audit.corrected: Rewritten in whys[3], spikes[1], mid, wants.you[0], wants.foe[0], dosFull[0].d, report[5].t and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'take the fifteen-second invitation' — invented number; and Empower was never mentioned.
audit.why: Counter Strike is 17/15/13/11/9 — 17s at rank 1. Empower is a 7-second auto-attack reset, the flagged missing interaction: the wind-up is the cue to step back, not the cast.
audit.corrected: 17s written in; Empower's reset added to breakdown.cooldowns.

edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are where the tide turns. With your full kit you can time the E2 hook to land while he's channeling Counter Strike — the pull stuns him out of his own dodge, your W fires into his missing-health threshold, and your heal covers the auto damage he already dealt. He can't burst you through the W if you're below half. At 6, Hijack copies Grandmaster's Might: you now have his R-stat armor and the passive proc burst he relies on, plus your own AP scaling on W. Force the all-in the moment Hijack comes off cooldown and deny him the first Trinity Force window by turning the lane into a kill.
edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are where the tide turns. Counter Strike dodges basic attacks, not abilities — so when he pops it, hold your autos, keep Chain Lash and Kingslayer flowing, and walk out of the 300-unit radius before the stun resolves. He spends 17 seconds of cooldown and you lose almost nothing. At 6, Hijack copies Grandmaster-at-Arms on 80 seconds against his own 110: you get the same armour and magic resist boost, and the burst around it, more often than he does. Force the all-in the moment Hijack is up and deny him the first Trinity Force window by turning the lane into a kill rather than a farm race.

notes: The packet reported zero defects here, but the page's central instruction — E2 hooking Jax to interrupt Counter Strike — was doubly wrong (Sylas's recast pulls him in and applies no CC; Counter Strike only dodges basic attacks anyway). That is the kind of line a player follows straight into a stun. Left alone deliberately: the 'no stun' phrasing in tradeBad, breakdown.trading, report[3].t and dontsFull[2].d, consistent with the mirror's decision to flag rather than guess.
